create.title: Create a course
create.intro: Answer a few questions, copy the prompt into a chat AI, then import its reply. Step by step, even a big course never gets cut off.
create.mode.label: What do you want to do?
create.preset.label: Start from
create.preset.examDesc: Built around your handouts and notes, with exam-style questions.
create.preset.programmingDesc: Code examples, reading and predicting code, typical bugs.
create.preset.understandDesc: Clear explanations with comparisons and worked examples.
create.preset.refresherDesc: Two short units in one reply, ideal before a test.
create.preset.deep-diveDesc: Many units, thorough lessons and a final exam.
create.preset.customDesc: Keep your current settings and adjust everything yourself.
create.subject: Subject
create.subjectHelp: Courses are grouped by subject in Explore and Progress.
create.priorHint: Binary numbers, what an IP address is
create.source.attached: I attach files in the chat (PDF, photos)
create.material: Your notes, handout text or slides
create.materialLong: That is a lot of text. Some chat tools cut long messages, so attaching the file can work better.
create.attachedHelp: Attach your files to the first message (the outline). Units are written in the same chat, so the AI can still see them.
create.strict.mainly: My material first, fill gaps with general knowledge (marked as extra)
create.cite: Show where each answer comes from (handout, page)
create.lang.bilingual: German and English, with a switch in each lesson
create.bilingualNote: Two languages make every reply about twice as long. Step-by-step mode keeps that manageable.
create.terms.primary: Keep exam terms in the main language
create.terms.both: Show the other language the first time
create.autoSize: Let the AI choose the size
create.gen.stepwise: Step by step: outline first, then one unit per reply (recommended)
create.gen.single: Everything in one reply (only for small courses)
create.operators: German exam task verbs (Operatoren, AFB I-III)
create.extra.videos: YouTube videos (in English, ready to play)
create.extra: Anything else the AI should know
create.extraHint: Use examples from a school network.
create.tip.chatgpt: ChatGPT: use a thinking model if you have one. It follows long instructions more reliably.
create.tip.claude: Claude: if the reply opens as a document on the side, copy it from there.
create.tip.gemini: Gemini: use the Pro model for long courses.
create.tip.deepseek: DeepSeek: turn on DeepThink for better questions.
create.tip.newChat: Start a new chat for each new course, then keep using that chat for its units.
create.tip.cutOff: If a reply stops in the middle, send: "Your reply was cut off. Write the same unit again, a bit shorter."
create.prompt.single: The whole course in one reply
create.how.2: Paste it into {tool} in a new chat.
create.how.2attached: Paste it into {tool} in a new chat and attach your files.
create.how.3: Copy the JSON it replies with.
create.how.5: Then open "Continue a course" here for the prompt of each unit.
create.needTopic: Enter a topic in step 1 first.
create.continue.none: Import an outline first. Its units show up here.
create.continue.help: Send these in the same chat as the outline, one at a time, and import each reply before the next.
create.savedSettings: Using the settings this course was created with.
create.currentSettings: This course was not planned here, so your current settings are used.
create.fix.hint: On the Import page, use "Copy errors", paste them here together with the reply, and send the fix prompt in the same chat.

quiz.warmupDone: Warm-up done. The lesson below explains the answers.
quiz.guessWrong: Good guess - here is the answer

challenge.title: Course challenge
challenge.cardText: Mixed questions from every unit of the course. The way to reach Mastered.
challenge.intro: {n} questions from the whole course, mixed together.
challenge.point.mixed: Up to {n} questions from every lesson, shuffled across units. Mixing topics makes you pick the right method yourself, which sticks better.
challenge.point.mastered: Proficient skills you answer completely right become Mastered.
challenge.point.drop: A wrong answer can lower a Proficient or Mastered skill by one level.
challenge.empty: This course has no practice questions yet.
settings.dailyReviewsHint: The most review questions offered in one day. After a break the rest come back over the next days instead of all at once.
settings.askConfidence: Ask "How sure are you?" before checking
settings.askConfidenceHint: Mistakes you were sure about come back sooner, and lucky guesses are not counted as learned.
create.checkHint: Copies a prompt for a fresh chat that double-checks this unit and sends back a corrected version to import.
create.checkHelp: Tip: open a NEW chat and use "Check" on a written unit. A second, separate check catches far more wrong answers than the AI checking its own work. Import the reply to replace the unit.
quiz.recallFirst: Recall first: think of the answer (or write it down) before you see the options. Remembering it yourself trains your memory much more than recognising it.
quiz.typo: Counted as right, but check the spelling: {answer}
results.levelUps: Level up! {n} skills reached a new level.
exercise.mixed: {n} questions from earlier lessons are mixed in, so you practise choosing the right method.
reflect.title: Reflect on this lesson
reflect.dumpIntro: Without scrolling up: write down everything you remember about "{topic}". Messy is fine. Then compare it with the key points and fill the gaps.
reflect.dumpIntroUnit: Without looking: write down everything you remember from the unit "{topic}". Then compare it with the key points of every lesson.
reflect.tickHint: Ticked automatically where your words match. Fix the ticks if they are wrong.
reflect.refine: Refine: read the {n} points in bold again, then try the brain dump once more tomorrow.
reflect.allCovered: You covered every key point. Try it again in a few days to make it stick.
reflect.copyDump: Ask an AI what I missed
reflect.explainIntro: Explain "{topic}" as if to a 12-year-old: simple words, one example, no step skipped. Where you get stuck or need jargon is where your understanding has a gap.
reflect.explainPlaceholder: Imagine you explain it to a friend...
reflect.jargon: These long words may be jargon. Can you say them more simply? {words}
reflect.check.example: Did you use a concrete example?
reflect.check.steps: Could someone follow every step without guessing?
reflect.check.gaps: Where did you hesitate? That part is worth reading again.
reflect.copyExplain: Let an AI ask me questions
home.goalReached: Daily goal reached: {n} energy points today.
stats.calibration: How well do you know what you know?
stats.calibrationHint: When you rate how sure you are, this compares your feeling with how often you were right.
stats.calibration.overconfident: You are often sure but wrong. Slow down on questions that feel easy, and test yourself instead of rereading.
stats.calibration.underconfident: You know more than you think: your unsure answers are mostly right. Trust yourself a bit more.
stats.calibration.calibrated: Your feeling of knowing is reliable: when you are sure, you are usually right.
stats.calibration.not-enough: Rate how sure you are on at least 10 answers to see how well your feeling matches your results.
settings.learningHint: Pick a study style, or set each option yourself.
settings.style.balancedHint: What works for most people: spaced reviews, How sure are you?, warm-ups and reflection.
settings.style.examHint: Remember as much as possible: more reviews, recall before options, no hints.
settings.style.deepHint: Understanding first: recall before options, brain dumps and explaining in your own words.
settings.style.relaxedHint: Low pressure: fewer reviews and fewer extra steps.
settings.style.custom: Custom: you changed single options below.
settings.retentionHint: The scheduler brings questions back just before you would forget them. Aiming higher means remembering more, but reviews grow quickly: 95% needs about twice as many as 90%.
settings.interleave: Mix in questions from earlier lessons
settings.interleaveHint: Mixed practice feels harder but sticks better, because you have to pick the right method yourself.
settings.recallFirstHint: Multiple choice hides the options until you have thought of an answer. Harder, and better for memory.
settings.allowHints: Offer hints and the full solution
settings.allowHintsHint: Turn off for exam practice. A hint still counts as not solved on the first try.
settings.acceptTypos: Accept small typos in typed answers
settings.showWarmupsHint: Guessing before you read, even wrongly, helps the lesson stick.
settings.showReflect: Brain dump and "explain it simply" after lessons
settings.showReflectHint: Write down what you remember and explain it in your own words: the most effective way to find what you do not understand yet.
settings.dailyGoalHint: A right answer gives 10, a finished lesson 5. The goal is separate from your streak.
settings.celebrations: Celebrate a new mastery level and a reached goal
settings.sounds: Soft sounds for right and wrong answers
settings.readingFont.hyperlegible: Atkinson Hyperlegible (easier to tell letters apart)
settings.courseIntro: These choices apply only to this course. Anything you leave alone follows your app settings.
settings.courseMissing: That course is not in your library any more, so these are the app settings.
settings.globalOnly: Reviews per day and the daily goal count across all courses, so they are only in the app settings.
settings.courseSectionHint: Give a course its own learning settings, for example exam prep for one subject and relaxed for another. Open a course and choose Course settings, or pick it at the top of this page.
settings.courseNone: No course has its own settings yet.
settings.layoutHint: Choose how much each screen shows and how much fits on it.
settings.layout.standardHint: Sidebars, cards and the usual amount of detail.
settings.layout.simpleHint: One column, big buttons, a tab bar and only what you need right now.
settings.layout.detailedHint: All the numbers: memory strength, points, question counts and reading time.
settings.layout.compactHint: Tight spacing and no extra explanations, so more fits on the screen.
settings.screenModeHint: On a phone or tablet the desktop layout shows the sidebars and the full header, scaled down. Pinch to zoom.
unit.totals: {lessons} lessons, {questions} questions, about {minutes} min of reading
chess.hint1: Look at checks, captures and threats first. The marked piece makes the move.
chess.goal.mateIn: checkmate the king in {n} moves or fewer.
chess.goal.promote: get a pawn to the last rank and promote it.
chess.result.won.held: You held the position. Well done.
chess.result.won.stalemate: Stalemate: a draw, and that was the goal.
chess.result.won.material: Draw by too little material, and that was the goal.
chess.result.won.repetition: Draw by repetition, and that was the goal.
chess.result.won.fifty: Draw by the fifty-move rule, and that was the goal.
chess.result.lost.mated: Checkmate. The computer won this one.
chess.result.lost.stalemate: Stalemate: the king has no move but is not in check, so it is a draw. Leave the king a square.
chess.result.lost.material: Draw: not enough material is left to checkmate.
chess.result.lost.repetition: Draw by repetition: the same position came up three times.
chess.result.lost.moves: Out of moves. Try again and look for a faster way.
chess.result.draw.stalemate: Stalemate. The game is a draw.
chess.result.draw.material: Draw: not enough material is left to checkmate.
chess.materialUp: You are {n} points of material up.
chess.materialDown: You are {n} points of material down.
chess.levelHint.1: Makes plenty of mistakes and often leaves pieces hanging.
chess.levelHint.2: Sees simple captures but misses a lot.
chess.levelHint.3: Punishes hanging pieces and simple tactics. A good partner on the way to 1000.
chess.levelHint.4: Calculates a few moves ahead and rarely blunders.
chess.levelHint.5: Thinks as deep as it can in two seconds.
play.title: Chess board
play.intro: Play a full game against the computer, or set up any position and play it out. Pick a strength that wins about half of the games against you.
play.badFen: That is not a playable position. Copy the FEN from chess.com or lichess (Share, then FEN).
play.fenHint: You can copy a position from chess.com or lichess: open the game, choose Share, then copy the FEN.

catalog.hint: Free courses that come with the app. Updating one keeps your progress.
catalog.failed: The course could not be added. Try again.
